Updated assessment with Beige Book: The FOMC’s cautiously accommodative stance remains appropriate. The latest Beige Book reports modest-to-moderate expansion across Districts, with consumer spending generally rising and energy activity improving alongside oil and natural gas. Labor markets are tight nationwide, with widespread reports of shortages of qualified workers that are constraining hiring and putting some upward pressure on wages. These growth and labor-tightness signals partially offset the dovish impulse from soft inflation. However, the latest SLOOS points to weaker loan demand in CRE and consumer credit and tighter standards for consumer, auto, and credit cards (with some easing in residential mortgages), implying downside risks to growth and inflation via credit channels. Net-net, the Fed’s patience is reinforced, balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon” remains a mild hawkish note, and financial conditions face only limited immediate restraint. Tone: slightly less bullish for duration than before given labor tightness, still only mildly constructive for risk assets given credit headwinds.

Updated excerpt: “Beige Book shows modest-to-moderate growth, rising consumer spending, improved energy activity, and tight labor markets with worker shortages and some wage pressures; paired with soft inflation and weaker loan demand/tighter consumer standards in SLOOS, the Fed stays patient with rates below neutral and proceeds gradually on balance-sheet normalization.”
